Unauthorized GitHub Workflow Trigger [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-284] on GitHub Source Repo, AWS CodeStar, AWS CodeBuild, App Runner ECR: Attackers can create pull requests or comment on existing PRs to trigger workflow runs. If not properly configured, forked repositories can also trigger workflows with access to secrets. An attacker forks the repository, modifies the workflow to exfiltrate secrets, and creates a PR to trigger the malicious workflow.

Container Image Vulnerabilities [Tampering, Information Disclosure, CWE-1104] on Customer ECR, App Runner Service, Fargate Tasks: Vulnerable container images may contain known CVEs in base images, application dependencies, or system packages that could be exploited once deployed. An attacker exploits a known vulnerability in an outdated package within the deployed container to achieve remote code execution.

Secrets and Configuration Exposure [Information Disclosure, CWE-798] on GitHub Source Repo, Secrets Manager, Parameter Store, CloudWatch Logs: Secrets can be exposed through committed code, environment variables in logs, or misconfigured access policies to AWS Secrets Manager. An attacker finds AWS credentials in Git history or CloudWatch logs, using them to access AWS resources.

DDoS and Resource Exhaustion [Denial of Service, CWE-400] on App Runner Service, Network Load Balancer, Route 53: Attackers can generate high volumes of traffic to trigger App Runner auto-scaling, leading to increased costs and potential service disruption. An attacker launches a DDoS attack causing App Runner to scale up significantly, resulting in unexpected costs.

VPC Network Security Misconfigurations [Information Disclosure, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-923] on Customer VPC, NAT Gateway, Internet Gateway, Security Groups: Overly permissive security groups, misconfigured route tables, or improperly configured network ACLs can expose services to unauthorized access. An attacker exploits overly permissive security group rules to access internal services that should not be exposed.

IAM Role and Permission Misconfigurations [Elevation of Privilege, CWE-269] on IAM Roles, App Runner Service, Secrets Manager, KMS: Overly permissive IAM roles or policies can allow services or users to access resources beyond their intended scope. An attacker exploits an overly permissive App Runner instance role to access sensitive data in other AWS services.

DNS-Based Attacks [Tampering, Denial of Service, CWE-350] on Route 53, Network Load Balancer, App Runner Service: Attackers can exploit DNS misconfigurations for zone enumeration, cache poisoning, or denial of service attacks. An attacker performs DNS zone walking to enumerate subdomains and identify potential targets.
